chapter_theme: The individual soul (சீவன்): it is unimaginably small, yet the Lord, greater than all, dwells within its flesh; bound by maya's adjuncts, it is stirred by the guru's grace, leaves them, enters the fourth state and becomes knowledge, and takes Siva's form within.

2011.reading: To tell the form of the soul: split a cow's hair into a hundred and each part into a thousand, and the soul's part is one in a hundred thousand.
2011.nuance: A similar measure of the soul by dividing a hair-tip is found in Upanishadic texts. The point is the soul's subtlety, not a literal size.

2012.reading: Though our Lord is greater than all others, he is mingled within the flesh in smallness and is there; Mahadeva is not of a measure the gods can know; his measure is known by tapas.
2012.nuance: The last line can be 'he alone knows the measure of tapas' or 'his measure is known only by tapas'. The verse balances greatness and smallness, answering 2011's tiny soul with the Lord who dwells in it.

2013.reading: He is, and he is clear; to speak of it, though souls lack the quality of practising separation, the souls who practised of old will later see and take Siva's form within their thought.
2013.nuance: வியோகம் (separation, or detachment) and the syntax of the first two lines are unclear; உண்டு தெளிவன் may also be 'having experienced, I am clear'. The last line, taking Siva's form in thought, is the firm part.

2014.reading: The conscious soul is under the sway of maya's adjuncts; when it is stirred there by the grace of the guru, the adjuncts cease, and the soul, not becoming one with them, enters turiya and becomes knowledge.
2014.nuance: உபாதி (limiting adjunct) and துரியம் (the fourth state, beyond waking, dream and deep sleep) are technical terms. ஒன்றின் ஒன்றாது may be 'not merging with what it joined'. The guru's grace as the trigger is plain.

source_issues: 2011 line 4: நாறாயிரத்து is read as நூறாயிரத்து (a hundred thousand).

links.note: 2012 and 490 are near-identical: though our Lord is greater than all (ஏனோர் பெருமையன்), he is mingled within the smallness of flesh (ஊனே சிறுமையுள் உட்கலந்து), beyond the gods' measure, known by tapas. The verse appears again in the chapter on the soul, where it answers 2011's soul measured as a hair split a hundred thousand ways.

2012 and 3024 are the same verse with small differences (தவத்தின் அளவே in both); the Lord great beyond all yet mingled in the flesh in smallness. Its third appearance, in the closing hymns, shows the verse working as a refrain across the book.
